questions.prompt: What is the main purpose of General Periods?
questions.answer: Fourier series can represent functions with period 2L rather than just 2 pi. The harmonics change from nx to n pi x divided by L so that each mode fits the interval.

questions.prompt: What does \(L\) mean in General Periods?
questions.answer: In General Periods, \(L\) means positive half-period. Its unit is same unit as x.

questions.prompt: Identify another important piece of notation used in General Periods.
questions.answer: In General Periods, \(2L\) means full period. Its unit is same unit as x.

questions.prompt: State a central formula or test for General Periods.
questions.answer:
The fourier series on negative l to l is
\[f(x)\sim\frac{a_0}{2}+\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}\left(a_n\cos\frac{n\pi x}{L}+b_n\sin\frac{n\pi x}{L}\right)\]
Use it only after the symbols in the formula have been identified for the specific general periods problem.

questions.prompt: How is the formula or method in General Periods interpreted rather than just memorised?
questions.answer:
Interpret the symbols and the condition being tested. The general-period coefficients is
\[a_n=\frac{1}{L}\int_{-L}^{L}f(x)\cos\frac{n\pi x}{L}\,dx\]
Use it only after the symbols in the formula have been identified for the specific general periods problem.

questions.prompt: Why do fixed-string boundary modes on the interval from 0 to L use sin n pi x over L?
questions.answer: This is a boundary-mode example on the interval from 0 to L, not the same setup as a periodic Fourier series on negative L to L. A fixed string has zero displacement at x=0 and x=L. The sine mode satisfies \[\sin\frac{n\pi 0}{L}=0\] and \[\sin\frac{n\pi L}{L}=\sin n\pi=0\] Thus each positive integer n gives a mode that fits the fixed-end boundary conditions.

questions.prompt: What changes in the coefficient formula when the interval is negative L to L?
questions.answer: The interval length changes, so the normalization changes from one over pi to one over L, and the mode argument changes from nx to n pi x over L: \[b_n=\frac{1}{L}\int_{-L}^{L}f(x)\sin\frac{n\pi x}{L}\,dx\]
